# P5: Sleep and memory in a lab

Citation: Okonkwo, B., et al. (2020). Learning and Sleep, 12(4), 301-315.
Type: lab experiment (n = 40 volunteers, aged 15 to 17)

Abstract: Volunteers learned word pairs, then slept either six or nine hours in the lab. Those who slept nine hours recalled 18 per cent more pairs the next morning. The sample is small and was tested in a quiet lab, not in school.

My notes: Neat result, but 40 students tells us little about a whole school.
